description: D-02 — Smart Home Business Dashboard. Answers: Is the Smart Home automation pipeline healthy? Covers dispatch throughput, action success/failure rates, provider performance, and business relationships (Scheduler/HTTP → Dispatch → Queue → Action). Business-scoped: no infrastructure or generic application metrics.

panels.description: Fraction of Smart Home action executions that succeeded (outcome=success). Healthy steady-state: > 95%. A drop below 90% is critical — drill into D-04 Queue Workers for queue health, then Tempo (filter by smart_home.action + outcome=failure) for trace detail.
panels.title: Action Success Rate

panels.description: Fraction of Smart Home action executions that failed (outcome=failure or unknown). Does NOT include unsupported — that is a distinct business outcome, not a failure. Above 5% warrants investigation. Note: ixora.queue.job.total{outcome=success} does NOT reflect this — see Business Relationships section (Phase 7B.4.5 §8.3).
panels.title: Action Failure Rate

panels.description: Fraction of actions rejected as unsupported (outcome=unsupported). This is a Business outcome, not a failure — it means the action type has no mapping in the current provider integration (e.g. Home Assistant ACTION_SERVICE_MAP). A non-zero rate means users have actions that the current MVP provider cannot execute. Investigation: Tempo filter smart_home.action + outcome=unsupported.
panels.title: Unsupported Action Rate

panels.description: Current rate of Smart Home action executions per second. Healthy: matches expected automation volume for the environment. A sustained drop to 0 while dispatches continue means the queue is not being consumed (check D-04 Queue Workers).
panels.title: Action Execution Rate

panels.description: Smart Home action success rate over time. Healthy: consistently above 95%. Use the time window to correlate drops with deployments or provider incidents. A persistent downward trend signals a recurring provider or configuration issue.
panels.title: Business Health Over Time (Success vs Failure Rate)

panels.description: Rate of Smart Home dispatch calls per second, split by entry point (manual=HTTP controller, scheduled=DispatchDueSchedulesCommand). Each dispatch call enqueues N actions and skips M actions — this panel counts dispatch call rate, not individual actions. A drop in 'scheduled' means the scheduler is not triggering Smart Home automations.
panels.title: Dispatch Rate by Entry Point

panels.description: Rate of actions dispatched vs skipped, across all entry points. 'dispatched' counts actions successfully enqueued; 'skipped' counts actions where the device relation was null at enqueue time (expected, async race condition — not an error per Phase 7B.4.5 §3.1). A high skip rate may indicate stale vibe_device_action rows.
panels.title: Dispatched vs Skipped Actions

panels.description: Rate of Smart Home action executions per second, split by provider. 'home_assistant' is the current MVP provider. 'future' is the reserved enum value for not-yet-integrated providers. A drop in 'home_assistant' while actions continue dispatching means queue depth is growing — check D-04.
panels.title: Action Rate by Provider

panels.description: Rate of Smart Home action executions, split by outcome: success (provider accepted), failure (provider rejected or transport error), unsupported (action type not in provider map), unknown (classifier degradation — should always be 0 in steady state). All four outcomes are distinct — do not conflate failure and unsupported.
panels.title: Action Rate by Outcome

panels.description: Rate of failed Smart Home action executions (outcome=failure). 'failure' conflates provider-side rejection (P2: non-2xx) and internally-caught transport errors (P3: ConnectionException). Both are counted as failure — the distinction requires Tempo drill-down (smart_home.provider span → Guzzle CLIENT span's http.response.status_code or recorded exception). Healthy: rate should be near 0.

links.title: Drill down: Tempo traces for failed actions

panels.title: Failed Actions Rate (by Provider)

panels.description: Rate of dispatch-level errors — failures at the VibeSmartHomeDispatchService::dispatch() boundary (D2: the DB query or enqueue itself threw). This rate should be near 0 in steady state; the dispatch service has no business-exception branch, so any error here is infrastructure (Phase 7B.4.5 §3.1). A non-zero rate requires checking DB/connection health (D-07).
panels.title: Dispatch Errors (by Entry Point)

panels.description: Action failure rate (failure + unknown outcomes / total) broken down by provider. Allows isolating whether a failure spike is provider-specific or global. A high failure rate for 'home_assistant' combined with a low failure rate overall is a Home Assistant availability incident. Healthy: < 5% per provider.
panels.title: Failure Rate by Provider

panels.description: Rate of actions rejected as unsupported, by provider. 'unsupported' is a Business outcome (not a failure — span stays OK). A non-zero rate means action_type values exist in the database that have no mapping in the provider's ACTION_SERVICE_MAP. Investigation: Tempo filter smart_home.action + outcome=unsupported; Loki warning logs from SmartHomeActionJob.
panels.title: Unsupported Actions by Provider

panels.description: Smart Home action execution latency percentiles (P50, P95, P99) in milliseconds. Measures the full business execution segment: ProviderAdapterResolver.forProvider() + HomeAssistantAdapter.executeAction() including the HTTP call to Home Assistant. Healthy: P95 < 2000 ms. A rising P99 while P50 is stable indicates tail-latency from slow provider responses.
panels.title: Action Latency Percentiles (p50 / p95 / p99)

panels.description: P95 action execution latency broken down by provider and outcome. Allows correlating latency changes with specific provider behavior or outcome patterns. A high P95 for 'home_assistant' indicates Home Assistant is responding slowly. A high P95 for 'failure' may indicate connection timeout exhaustion (P3: ConnectionException after timeout).
panels.title: P95 Latency by Provider

panels.description: P95 action execution latency broken down by outcome. High latency for 'failure' compared to 'success' suggests failure paths involve timeout exhaustion (ConnectionException converted to ActionResult failure). High latency for 'success' indicates the provider itself is slow. Note: Tempo trace duration (smart_home.action span) for a specific attempt provides exact timing detail.
panels.title: P95 Latency by Outcome

panels.description: Action execution duration distribution as a heatmap. Each column is a time bucket; each row is a histogram bucket (ms). Darker cells = more observations at that duration. Useful for visualizing bimodal distributions (fast successes + slow timeouts) or distribution shifts over time. Trace retention: 7 days (ADR-031).
panels.title: Action Duration Heatmap

panels.description: Dispatch call rate split by entry point over time. 'manual' = dispatches triggered by HTTP API (VibeSmartHomeDispatchController); 'scheduled' = dispatches triggered by DispatchDueSchedulesCommand (cron/scheduler). Together they represent all Smart Home automation triggers. A drop in 'scheduled' may indicate a Scheduler issue (check D-06). A drop in 'manual' may indicate an API issue (check D-05).

links.title: D-05 HTTP API (for manual entry point)

panels.title: Dispatch Flow — Scheduled vs Manual

panels.description: Queue job outcomes for SmartHomeActionJob alongside Smart Home action outcomes. CRITICAL: ixora_queue_job_total{outcome='success'} means 'the job process completed without crashing' — it does NOT mean the Smart Home action itself succeeded. SmartHomeActionJob::handle() swallows every exception, so Queue outcome=success is expected even when action outcome=failure. See Phase 7B.4.5 §8.3 for full explanation. Do not correlate these two metrics without this context.
panels.title: Queue Workers → Smart Home (Orthogonality)

panels.description: Total number of Smart Home action executions in the selected time window, broken down by provider. Shows the relative volume of each provider integration. 'home_assistant' is the current MVP provider. Useful for capacity planning and provider-specific issue scoping.
panels.title: Provider Distribution (in selected time window)

panels.description: Total Smart Home actions in the selected time window broken down by all outcomes: success, failure, unsupported, unknown. Provides a business pipeline summary view. 'unsupported' actions are a product gap — users have actions the current MVP provider cannot execute. 'unknown' actions indicate a telemetry classifier failure and should always be 0.
panels.title: Business Pipeline Summary (in selected time window)

list.description: Deployment environment — applied to all panel queries.
list.label: Environment
list.name: environment

list.description: Smart Home provider filter — applied to action metrics. Values are bounded: home_assistant (current MVP), future (reserved for additional integrations).
list.label: Provider
list.name: provider
